patch_description: Instead of pure greedy restarts followed by a single 2-opt pass, I implement a GRASP-style framework: (1) beam search construction that keeps multiple partial schedules alive at each step, allowing recovery from greedy mistakes; (2) repeated randomized-greedy restarts with a restricted candidate list; (3) local search on every promising candidate using both 2-opt segment reversal and insertion moves (moving a txn to a different position, which 2-opt cannot do); (4) perturbation kicks (random double-bridge moves) from the incumbent to escape local optima, accepting only improvements. The key insight is that 2-opt reversal alone is weak for this problem—relocating a single conflicted transaction often reduces makespan far more—so combining insertion moves with kick-based restarts from good solutions beats searching from scratch each time.
